chunks: And Al-Alaa narrated from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever is killed defending his wealth is a martyr.' He (the Imam) said: 'And he said: If it were me, I would have abandoned the wealth and not fought.'

key_terms.أَحَدِهِمَا: One of the two (referring to the two Imams, typically Muhammad ibn al-Hasan and his brother, or generally the Imams)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a person killed while defending their property in Islam?
ai.summary: This narration from Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih illustrates the nuanced Shia jurisprudence on martyrdom, distinguishing between the legal status of being a 'shahid' for defending wealth and the spiritual merit of voluntary renunciation (zuhd). The apparent contradiction is resolved by scholars who view the combatant as a martyr by virtue of the struggle, while the one who leaves wealth demonstrates a higher degree of detachment from worldly attachments, reflecting the Imam's personal preference for peace over conflict.
